subject: Dedicated capacity pricing qualification: GPU type, reserved size, throughput targets
messages:
From: Aisha Khan <aisha.k@finlytics.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 26 Feb 2026 15:02:00 -0800
Subject: Follow-up: Dedicated capacity discussion + numbers

Hi Marissa / Marcus —

Thanks again for the demo and the deep-dive today. Quick recap from our side and a couple asks so we can move to pricing: 

- Workload mix: 70% chat assistant (multi-turn convs, avg request = ~450 tokens/user call), 30% batch summarization jobs (avg 8k tokens per job).
- Expected steady-state volume: ~250M tokens/day in Q4 first 6 months; spiky peaks up to ~500M tokens/day during end-of-month reporting.
- Latency target for chat: 200–400ms tail; throughput target for batch: ~1200 tokens/sec sustained for summarization jobs.
- Preferred models: open Llama-3 family and context length up to 32k for summarization.
- Initial procurement timeline: decision in two weeks, target start of reserved capacity by end of next month.

Budget range: $30k–$60k/month committed for dedicated capacity (this is for hardware + Redwood managed service). We are flexible if unit economics hit our target of approximately $100–$150 per 1M tokens.

Could you confirm:
1) Recommended GPU type/config for this workload (A100 80GB vs H100 or equivalent)
2) Suggested reserved capacity size to meet steady-state + spiky peaks (ballpark # of GPUs)
3) Estimated $/1M tokens and monthly committed cost ranges for the recommended config

I attached an export of our recent usage slices to help with sizing (finlytics_usage_export.csv).

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick call if easier.

— Aisha
Aisha Khan
Head of Data Products, FinLytics
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Aisha Khan <aisha.k@finlytics.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 1 Mar 2026 09:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Dedicated capacity discussion + numbers

Hi Aisha —

Appreciate the clear numbers and the CSV — that helps a lot. Short recap from our side and a few clarifying Qs before Marcus and I put together a formal sizing + pricing pack: 

Recap:
- 250M tokens/day steady-state (~7.5B tokens/month), peaks to 500M/day.
- Latency target ~200–400ms tail for chat.
- Models: Llama-3 family, up to 32k context for summarization.

Clarifying Qs:
1) For the chat traffic, what percentage is real-time vs background processing? (i.e., do you allow slightly higher latency for a subset of requests that could be batched?)
2) Do you have a hard SLO on 99th percentile latency or is 95th the primary metric?
3) For summarization, are jobs time-sensitive or can they be queued (helps with batching economics)?

Next steps: Marcus will draft two recommended configs (A: lower-latency H100-focused, B: A100 80GB optimized for cost/throughput) with attendant unit economics ($/1M tokens) and monthly committed pricing ranges. We'll include assumptions (avg tokens per call, cache hit rate, batching factors).

Attaching our preliminary pricing template so you can see the fields we'll fill (redwood-dedicated-pricing-v1.pdf). Can you confirm a good time next week for a 30-min sizing call?

Best,
Marissa Cole
Director, Sales Engineering — Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Aisha Khan <aisha.k@finlytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 2 Mar 2026 10:45:00 -0800
Subject: Suggested configs + ballpark economics (preliminary)

Hey Aisha —

Per our thread and Marissa's notes, here's a quick preliminary sizing and economics view. These are ballpark numbers we use for initial qualification; we'll refine after the sizing call and by looking at the CSV in detail.

Option A — H100-prioritized (lower latency):
- Config: 4x H100 SXM3 (reserved) + Redwood routing/replicas for redundancy
- Expected steady throughput (chat-heavy, <400ms tail): ~400–600K tokens/sec aggregate across the pool for short-context workloads
- Batch summarization: can sustain ~1.2–1.5M tokens/sec when jobs are scheduled
- Estimated unit cost: $90–$120 per 1M tokens (assumes moderate caching and 1.2x batching efficiency)
- Estimated monthly committed cost: $45k–$75k/month (includes reserved GPU amortization + Redwood management + premium SLAs)

Option B — A100 80GB (cost-optimized):
- Config: 8x A100 80GB (reserved) with aggressive batching and prefix caching
- Expected steady throughput: ~350–500K tokens/sec aggregate for chat; batch summarization ~1.0–1.3M tokens/sec
- Estimated unit cost: $70–$100 per 1M tokens (higher batching and slightly lower HW cost)
- Estimated monthly committed cost: $30k–$55k/month

Assumptions and notes:
- Unit economics normalized to your stated mix (70% chat, 30% batch) and to 7.5B tokens/month steady-state. If peaks require headroom, add burst capacity (on-demand GPUs) or increase reserved pool size.
- 99th pct latency for chat on H100 config should be materially better (~200–350ms) vs A100 (~300–500ms) depending on model/config and KV cache hit rate.
- We can tighten $/1M tokens by increasing cache hit rates, model quantization, or accepting longer tail latencies for a portion of chat traffic.

Next step: propose a 30-min call tomorrow or Wed to lock assumptions and run a quick cost calc against your CSV. If you want, we can also prepare a 12-month reserved commitment quote vs 3-month to show savings.

— Marcus
Principal Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 3 Mar 2026 14:05:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Suggested configs + ballpark economics (preliminary)

Looping in briefly — from an infra perspective the two configs above look sound. Key trade-offs to call out for the call:
- If FinLytics expects sustained 500M token/day peaks regularly, we should size with ~30% headroom (i.e., opt for the larger reserved pool or plan on burst capacity).
- Network egress for large summarization jobs may push us to choose more GPUs per rack to optimize intra-rack NVLink throughput for long-context runs.
- We'll come with some example throughput tests for Llama-3-32k in both quantized and non-quantized modes so the call can go into specifics.

I can join the sizing call and run through expected perf numbers — available Wed 11–1pt or Thu afternoon.

— Rishi (Infra)
From: Aisha Khan <aisha.k@finlytics.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 4 Mar 2026 11:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Suggested configs + ballpark economics (preliminary)

Thanks everyone — this is very helpful. We're aligned on the trade-offs. A few quick answers and next steps from our side: 

- Real-time vs background: ~85% of chat is real-time; ~15% can be batched (non-urgent analytics).
- SLO: 99th pct is important for customer-facing sessions, aiming for <400ms.
- Summarization jobs can be queued up to 3–5 minutes; batching is OK here.

Budget: we were expecting $30k–$60k/month as a committed range and your Option B numbers (A100-based) look like the right starting point. If A gives us better 99th pct latency for not-much-more then we'll consider it.

Let's schedule the 30-min sizing call Thu at 11:30am PT. I'll send a calendar invite. We'll need a simple committed quote (3- and 12-month) and a draft mutual action plan so procurement can start the internal approval. Also please add a DocuSign link / purchase order template when you send the quote.

I've attached a small sample of payloads and an example SLA request (finlytics_example_payloads.zip).

DocuSign: https://docusign.com/fake/FinLytics-Redwood-DL-1289
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/12345/DL-1289

Thanks — Aisha
